components.note: Water — 浅 originally described shallow water.
Gives the sound qiǎn, matching the character's reading.

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé hěn qiǎn.
example.english: This river is very shallow.
example.fact: 浅 is the opposite of 深 (deep), often describing water or knowledge.

components.note: Offering/enjoying — links to the idea of sincere giving.
Gives a sound distantly related to dūn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè dūnhòu de rén.
example.english: He is a sincere and kind person.

etymologyHint: To connect 丩 threads 纟; 丩 also provides the pronunciation

Depicts two threads winding around each other, hence 'entangle.'

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiūzhèng le wǒ de fāyīn.
example.english: The teacher corrected my pronunciation.

components.note: Metal — 钻 relates to a metal tool, a drill.

example.pinyin: Gōngrén zài qiáng shàng zuān le yí gè dòng.
example.english: The worker drilled a hole in the wall.
example.fact: 钻 is a verb meaning 'to drill' or 'to bore through.'

etymologyHint: Many suns 日, suggesting a bright and glittering gem

components.note: The sun 日 shape appears three times, stacked to suggest a sparkling crystal.

example.pinyin: Shuǐjīng hěn piàoliang.

components.note: Gives the sound jǐ, related to qǐ through an older reading before the sounds drifted apart.

etymologyHint: The space between 夹 two mountains 山; 夹 also provides the pronunciation

example.english: The Three Gorges of the Yangtze River are very famous.
example.fact: 峡 means 'gorge' or 'strait,' as in 三峡 (Sānxiá), the famous Three Gorges.

components.note: Grass/plant — links to natural green or blue-green colors.
Gives the sound cāng, matching the character's reading.

example.pinyin: Tā de liǎnsè hěn cāngbái.

meanings: to spout; to spurt; to spray; to puff

example.english: This computer uses a lot of electricity.
example.fact: 耗 means 'to consume' or 'use up,' often about energy or resources.

components.note: Ice — related to the character's early sense of cold.
Gives the sound líng, matching the character's reading.

example.english: He gets up at three in the morning.
example.fact: 凌 often appears in 凌晨 (língchén), meaning 'the early hours before dawn.'

Gives the sound gāo, related to qiāo but drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 敲 means 'to knock' or 'to strike,' as in 敲门 (qiāo mén), 'to knock on a door.'

Gives the sound qūn, related to jūn but drifted apart over time.

example.english: Washing hands can kill germs.

Gives the sound pǒu, related to péi but drifted apart over time.

Gives the sound yú, related to tú but drifted apart over time.

Gives the sound zú, related to cuì but drifted apart over time.

example.english: This box is very flat.

components.note: Roof — a house shut in quiet stillness.

example.fact: 熊 means 'bear,' a large, strong animal.

components.note: Water — relates directly to wetness.

example.fact: 暖 means 'warm,' often used as 暖和 (nuǎnhuo), 'warm and cozy.'

components.note: Grain — originally related to arranging harvested grain in order.

components.note: Cloth/towel — hats are made of cloth.
Gives the sound mào, matching the character's reading.

components.note: Mouth — associated with crying out in grief.
Gives a sound distantly related to āi, having drifted apart over time.

Gives the sound tà, matching the character's reading.

etymologyHint: A person 口 wearing a robe 衣

components.note: Hand — shaking is often done with the hands.

components.note: Mouth — sounds like scolding, yawning, or laughing come from the mouth.
Gives the sound kě, related to ā but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Ā, yuánlái shì nǐ!
example.english: Oh, it's you!
example.fact: 呵 is used as an exclamation of surprise, similar to 'oh!' in English.

components.note: Speech — litigation involves speaking/arguing a case.
Gives the sound gōng, related to sòng but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这是一场很复杂的诉讼。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì chǎng hěn fùzá de sùsòng.
example.english: This is a very complicated lawsuit.
example.fact: 讼 means 'lawsuit' or 'litigation,' as in 诉讼 (sùsòng).

components.note: Gas — oxygen is a type of gas.
Gives the sound yáng, related to yǎng but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen hūxī xūyào yǎngqì.
example.english: We need oxygen to breathe.
example.fact: 氧 means 'oxygen,' as in 氧气 (yǎngqì).

components.note: Water — originally described a vast expanse of water.
Gives the sound gào, related to hào but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè hàodà de gōngchéng.
example.english: This is a massive project.
example.fact: 浩 means 'vast' or 'grand,' as in 浩大 (hàodà).

components.note: One side of a feather/wing shape.
The mirrored other side, together forming a pair of wings.

example.pinyin: Niǎo shēn shàng yǒu hěn duō yǔmáo.
example.english: Birds have many feathers on their bodies.
example.fact: 羽 means 'feather,' as in 羽毛 (yǔmáo).

example.pinyin: Zhè kuài ròu yǒu yì jīn.
example.english: This piece of meat weighs one catty.
example.fact: 斤 is a traditional Chinese unit of weight, about 500 grams.

components.note: Wine — the original sense described the strong taste of wine.
Gives the sound gào, related to kù but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié kànqǐlái hěn kù.
example.english: These shoes look very cool.
example.fact: 酷 originally meant 'strong' or 'harsh,' but today is often borrowed to mean 'cool.'

components.note: Hand — plundering involves taking things by hand.
Gives the sound jīng, related to lüè but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shìbīng lüèduó le cūnzhuāng.
example.english: The soldiers plundered the village.
example.fact: 掠 means 'to plunder' or 'to rob,' as in 掠夺 (lüèduó).

components.note: Woman — many supernatural spirits in old stories were depicted as female.
Gives the sound yāo, matching the character's reading.

example.hanzi: 这个故事里有一个妖怪。
example.pinyin: Zhège gùshi lǐ yǒu yí gè yāoguài.
example.english: There is a goblin in this story.
example.fact: 妖 means 'goblin' or 'supernatural being,' as in 妖怪 (yāoguài).

components.note: Spirit — disasters were once thought to come from spirits or gods.
Gives the sound wō, related to huò but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng dàhuǒ shì yì chǎng zāihuò.
example.english: This big fire was a disaster.
example.fact: 祸 means 'disaster' or 'misfortune,' as in 灾祸 (zāihuò).

components.note: Person — describes a person who serves.
Gives the sound sì, related to shì but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 她一直服侍生病的奶奶。
example.pinyin: Tā yīzhí fúshì shēngbìng de nǎinai.
example.english: She has been attending to her sick grandmother.
example.fact: 侍 means 'to attend upon' or 'to serve,' as in 服侍 (fúshì).

components.note: The single curved stroke traces the shape of a swallow's body in flight.

example.hanzi: 在这次考试中,他得了乙等。
example.pinyin: Zài zhè cì kǎoshì zhōng, tā dé le yǐděng.
example.english: In this exam, he got a B grade.
example.fact: 乙 is the second of the ten heavenly stems, often used like 'B' to mark second place or grade.

components.note: Woman — an old semantic root, not directly related to the modern meaning.
Gives the sound fāng, related to fáng but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 噪音妨碍了我们的学习。
example.pinyin: Zàoyīn fáng'ài le wǒmen de xuéxí.
example.english: The noise hindered our studying.
example.fact: 妨 means 'to hinder,' as in 妨碍 (fáng'ài).

meanings: to have a voracious desire for

components.note: Money/shell — greed is often about wanting money.
Gives the sound jīn, related to tān but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhège rén hěn tānxīn.
example.english: This person is very greedy.
example.fact: 贪 means 'greedy,' as in 贪心 (tānxīn).

meanings: used in 掙扎|挣扎[zheng1 zha2]
etymologyHint: To fight 争 by hand 扌; 争 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: Hand — shows this is a physical action.
Represents fighting or striving for something.

example.pinyin: Tā zài shuǐ lǐ zhēngzhá.
example.english: He struggled in the water.
example.fact: 挣 means 'to struggle,' as in 挣扎 (zhēngzhá).

components.note: Water — describes a vast expanse of water.
Gives the sound wáng, related to wāng but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu wāngwāng de jiào.
example.english: The puppy barks 'woof woof.'
example.fact: 汪 is also used in 汪汪 (wāngwāng), the sound of a dog barking.

etymologyHint: A person, crouched 尸 passing water 水

components.note: A person's crouching body shape.
Water — represents the liquid being passed.

example.pinyin: Xiǎoháizi wǎnshang huì niàochuáng.
example.english: Children sometimes wet the bed at night.
example.fact: 尿 means 'urine' or 'to urinate.'

meanings: used in the transliteration of female names

components.note: Plant — jasmine is a flowering plant.
Gives the sound lì, matching the character's reading.

example.pinyin: Mòlihuā hěn xiāng.
example.english: Jasmine flowers are very fragrant.
example.fact: 莉 only appears in 茉莉 (mòli), 'jasmine.'

etymologyHint: Pride 心  in one's country 县, expressed by a flag; 县 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: Heart — links to a state of worry, later meaning something left hanging.
Suggests a place or symbol displayed high, like something hung up.

example.pinyin: Guóqí xuánguà zài qígān shàng.
example.english: The national flag hangs on the flagpole.
example.fact: 悬 means 'to hang' or 'to suspend,' as in 悬挂 (xuánguà).

components.note: Mouth — lips surround the mouth.
Gives the sound chén, related to chún but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā de chún hěn hóng.
example.english: Her lips are very red.
example.fact: 唇 means 'lips.'

components.note: Feather/plume — old writing brushes were made of feathers.
Gives the sound gàn, related to hàn but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Hàn cháng yòng zài rén de míngzi lǐ.
example.english: 翰 is often used in people's given names.
example.fact: 翰 originally meant 'writing brush' and today is common in personal names.

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 倉; grains 食 kept in storage 口

components.note: The roof-like top of a storage building.
Represents the enclosed space inside, where grain is stored.

example.pinyin: Huòwù fàng zài cāngkù lǐ.
example.english: The goods are stored in the warehouse.
example.fact: 仓 means 'storehouse,' as in 仓库 (cāngkù).

components.note: Cart/vehicle — tracks are made by wheels.
Gives the sound jiǔ, related to guǐ but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Huǒchē zài guǐdào shàng xíngshǐ.
example.english: The train runs on the track.
example.fact: 轨 means 'track' or 'rail,' as in 轨道 (guǐdào).

meanings: classifier for bombs, missiles, satellites etc

components.note: Tree — originally referred to a tree trunk or stalk.
Gives a sound distantly related to méi, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā mǎi le yì méi jièzhi.
example.english: He bought a ring.
example.fact: 枚 is a measure word used for small round objects, like rings or coins.

example.hanzi: 做菜的时候要放一点盐。
example.pinyin: Zuò cài de shíhòu yào fàng yìdiǎn yán.
example.english: You should add a little salt when cooking.
example.fact: 盐 means 'salt.'

components.note: See — looking at something involves the eyes/seeing.

example.hanzi: 我们去看了一个艺术展览。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen qù kàn le yí gè yìshù zhǎnlǎn.
example.english: We went to see an art exhibition.
example.fact: 览 means 'to view,' as in 展览 (zhǎnlǎn), 'exhibition.'

etymologyHint: Someone 亻 who lectures 尃; 尃 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: Person — represents someone who teaches.
Suggests spreading knowledge, related to instructing others.

example.hanzi: 他是一位很有经验的师傅。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi hěn yǒu jīngyàn de shīfu.
example.english: He is a very experienced master craftsman.
example.fact: 傅 means 'tutor' or 'teacher,' as in 师傅 (shīfu).

etymologyHint: An army officer carrying a weapon 刂 and a flag 巾

components.note: A flag — a symbol carried by a military leader.
A weapon, showing this person's role as a military commander.

example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de hěn shuài.
example.english: He looks very handsome.
example.fact: 帅 originally meant 'military commander,' and today commonly means 'handsome.'

etymologyHint: A building 广 containing an altar 由

components.note: Building — shows a structure or shelter.
Represents an altar or shrine placed inside.

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò miào hěn gǔlǎo.
example.english: This temple is very old.
example.fact: 庙 means 'temple' or 'shrine.'

components.note: Plant — fragrance often comes from flowers and plants.
Gives the sound fēn, matching the character's reading.

example.hanzi: 花园里满是芬芳的花朵。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ mǎn shì fēnfāng de huāduǒ.
example.english: The garden is full of fragrant flowers.
example.fact: 芬 means 'fragrance,' as in 芬芳 (fēnfāng).

meanings: used in 屏營|屏营[bing1 ying2]

components.note: Door — a screen is a barrier like a door.
Gives the sound bìng, related to píng but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Shǒujī píngmù huài le.
example.english: The phone screen is broken.
example.fact: 屏 means 'screen,' as in 屏幕 (píngmù).

etymologyHint: An offering 土 in your hand 寸

components.note: A hand shape, holding something.
Represents an offering placed in the hand, related to worship at a temple.

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò sìyuàn hěn yǒumíng.
example.english: This temple is very famous.
example.fact: 寺 means 'temple' or 'monastery,' as in 寺院 (sìyuàn).

components.note: Flesh — being fat relates to the body.
Gives the sound bàn, related to pàng but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā chī de tài duō, biàn pàng le.
example.english: He ate too much and became fat.
example.fact: 胖 means 'fat' or 'plump,' the opposite of 瘦 (thin).

components.note: Jade — an old semantic group for stone/gem-like materials, including glass.
Gives the sound lí, matching the character's reading.

example.pinyin: Bēizi shì bōli zuò de.
example.english: The cup is made of glass.
example.fact: 璃 only appears in 玻璃 (bōli), 'glass.'

components.note: Heart/mind — foolishness is related to one's mind.
Gives the sound yú, matching the character's reading.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè yúchǔn de juédìng.
example.english: This is a stupid decision.
example.fact: 愚 means 'foolish,' as in 愚蠢 (yúchǔn).

meanings: to let drip; to apply (eye drops etc)

components.note: Water — a drip involves water or liquid.
Gives the sound dí, related to dī but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 水从水龙头里一滴一滴地流下来。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ cóng shuǐlóngtóu lǐ yì dī yì dī de liú xiàlái.
example.english: Water drips down drop by drop from the faucet.
example.fact: 滴 means 'to drip' and is also a measure word for drops.

etymologyHint: Walking 疋 through uncultivated land 㐬

components.note: Foot/leg shape — represents walking.
Suggests scattered, uncultivated land, giving a sense of something sparse.

example.hanzi: 他因为疏忽忘记了带钱包。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi shūhu wàngjì le dài qiánbāo.
example.english: He forgot to bring his wallet due to carelessness.
example.fact: 疏 means 'careless' or 'sparse,' as in 疏忽 (shūhu), 'negligence.'

components.note: Solemn — links to a dejected or solemn mood.
Gives a sound distantly related to xiāo, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Jīngjì hěn xiāotiáo.
example.english: The economy is very depressed.
example.fact: 萧 means 'desolate' or 'dejected,' as in 萧条 (xiāotiáo).

components.note: Woman — beauty and appearance are often linked to this root.
Gives the sound cì, related to zī but drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā zhàn zhe de zīshì hěn hǎokàn.
example.english: Her standing posture looks very nice.
example.fact: 姿 means 'posture' or 'appearance,' as in 姿势 (zīshì).

components.note: Leaf/head — an old semantic root used generically for head/body actions.
Gives a sound distantly related to chàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā lěng de quánshēn chàndǒu.
example.english: He trembled all over from the cold.
example.fact: 颤 means 'to tremble' or 'to shiver,' as in 颤抖 (chàndǒu).
